title: Height formula expressed at a prime of the fibre ring
statement: Let R and S be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with a flat R-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let p be a prime of R, C = p.Fiber S = kappa(p) tensor_R S, Q a prime of C, and q its inverse image under S -> C. Localizations and fibre rings are as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then height(q) = height(p) + height(Q). Height is the dimension of the prime localization [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Proof of Tag 0339, with Tags 0337, 00ON, and Remark 0H9M; the fibre identifications are Mathlib Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂.

proof.text: Put q = Q.comap(includeRight). It lies over p. Equip S_q with the canonical R_p-algebra from the induced local map; flatness localizes and implies going down.

Apply Mathlib Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown to the maximal ideals of R_p and S_q. The heights of these ideals equal the respective Krull dimensions, hence height(p) and height(q).

The image I of the source maximal ideal is pS_q by map composition. This ideal is proper since the map is local. Thus the quotient is nontrivial and local; the surjective quotient map carries the target maximal ideal to the quotient maximal ideal, whose height is its Krull dimension.

Identify C_Q with S_q/I by Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂ and quotient equivalences for equal ideals. A ring isomorphism preserves Krull dimension. The dimension of C_Q equals height(Q). Substitute in step 2 and remove the injective coercion from extended naturals into WithBot extended naturals.

theorem height_eq_add_of_flat_fiber {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Algebra R S] (hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat)
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [Q.IsPrime] :
    (Q.comap Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom).height = p.height + Q.height

blueprint_update.statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of Noetherian commutative rings. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$, let $C=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS$ be the fibre ring over $\mathfrak p$, let $Q$ be a prime ideal of $C$, and let $\mathfrak q\subseteq S$ be its inverse image under $S\to C$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{ht}(Q)$.

proof.text: *Step 1.* The prime $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak p$. The induced map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, so it satisfies going down.

*Step 2.* For a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with going down, $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$. Here $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p$ and $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q$.

*Step 3.* The ideal $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ is proper since the map is local, and $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ is identified with the localization $C_Q$ of the fibre ring $C=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS$ at $Q$. Its dimension is $\operatorname{ht}Q$. Substituting into Step 2 gives $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p+\operatorname{ht}Q$.
